definition: Incontrovertible means impossible to dispute or deny; beyond argument.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word incontrovertible. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know incontrovertible should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The flight recorder settled the inquiry in a single afternoon: its data was incontrovertible, and the theories that had filled three months of hearings simply stopped.
Persuasive is weaker than incontrovertible: a persuasive case wins most listeners over but still leaves an opening to argue back, while incontrovertible evidence closes the argument outright.
Self-evident goes further than incontrovertible: incontrovertible claims are settled by overwhelming proof, but a self-evident truth needs no proof at all — doubting it barely makes sense.

Undeniable is the everyday word for what no honest person can reject, and it stretches to feelings and impressions — undeniable charm, undeniable talent. Incontrovertible is the courtroom-and-laboratory version: it claims a proof so complete that formal dispute itself has nowhere left to stand.

Irrefutable measures a claim against attack: every rebuttal that can be raised will fail. Incontrovertible describes the settled aftermath, the point where reasonable people stop treating the question as open. An argument is irrefutable; a fact is incontrovertible.

For decades, two museums claimed to own the true version of a small Dutch winter scene, and two sets of scholars built careers arguing the point.
Then a conservator suggested the obvious: the picture was painted on an oak panel, and oak keeps a diary.
Tree rings in the wood could be matched, year by year, against a master chronology for the Baltic timber trade.
The result was incontrovertible.
The panel in Antwerp came from a tree felled thirty years after the painter's death.
